comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C42, C46-C51 regarding generation and validation of the double-conditional knockout allele. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes specific data elements (dose-dependent effects, tissue specificity), while peer reviewers highlight this as a major strength with multiple reviewers praising the novel genetic model.

Perfect agreement on claims C52-C55 regarding mortality data. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval details the statistical analysis (p<0.0001, n=40 per group), while peer reviewers accepted the mortality findings without challenge and noted the assessments as 'well-powered and convincing.'

Perfect agreement on claims C56-C62 regarding electrophysiological phenotyping. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor (Welch t-test, n=7) and specificity to VCS, while peer reviewers praised the 'detailed electrophysiological phenotyping' and 'very robust functional data' without raising concerns.

Agreement on claims C63-C69 regarding preserved cardiac structure and function. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive data from echocardiography, histology, and qRT-PCR. Peer reviewers accepted the data but suggested lineage tracing would strengthen future work, though they did not challenge the presented findings.

Significant disagreement on claims C70-C74 regarding molecular characterization and transcriptional reprogramming. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical corrections, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, citing limited gene panel (only 2 genes assessed vs genome-wide), lack of direct comparison to working myocardium, and absence of key regulators like Irx3 and Nkx2-5. Reviewers suggested RNA-seq would provide clearer evidence.

Disagreement on claims C77-C80, C85 regarding optical mapping evidence for loss of VCS-specific conduction. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on loss of dual upstroke pattern (n=8-10 animals). Peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, noting alternative interpretations exist (focal bundle branch block vs actual cell fate change) and questioning tissue penetration depth and whether the AV bundle vs more superficial structures were actually visualized.

Disagreement on claims C81-C84 regarding preserved working myocardium function. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED showing specificity of VCS defect. Peer reviewers marked the broader optical mapping interpretation UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the data definitively distinguish between proximal bundle branch block versus true VCS cell fate transformation, and suggesting lineage tracing is needed.

Disagreement on main conclusions C110-C112 regarding VCS-to-working myocardium transformation. OpenEval finds the conclusion SUPPORTED by collective evidence. Peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 stating 'some key experiments that could more definitively test this model were not performed' and noting the data may reflect distinct rather than coordinated roles. However, the editor found conclusions 'supported by convincing data,' showing mixed peer assessment.
OpenEval evaluated claims C1, C44-C45 regarding genomic locations as SUPPORTED verifiable facts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C39-C41, C95-C97 summarizing prior published work as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature summary claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C99-C100, C103-C105 summarizing prior published work as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual literature claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C106-C109 comparing double-knockout to single knockouts as SUPPORTED, noting the interpretation is well-justified by collective data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this interpretation relates to concerns raised in R7 about the strength of cell fate transformation claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C2-C4, C16-C38 as SUPPORTED background knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these extensive background/context claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C113-C115 regarding methodological details as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these procedural claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C75-C76, C101-C102 regarding established technical knowledge as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background technical claims.

Peer reviewers evaluated claims C15, C43, C92-C94 (in addition to C110-C112) regarding main conclusions as UNCERTAIN, citing gap between evidence and mechanistic claims. OpenEval did not create a separate evaluation grouping these additional claims with the main conclusions, though R8 addresses C110-C112.
